logline: 고양이 한 마리가 장화와 자루와 꾀만으로 막내를 후작으로 만든다
destination: 동화 장화 신은 고양이에서 만날 수 있습니다
anchor: a Korean boy of about ten in hemp clothes, his small sister beside him
palette: hay gold, royal blue, crimson red, cream, moss green

beats.visual: the dusty mill yard in morning sun: the youngest son sits on an overturned crate outside the old stone watermill, patched shirt, chin in his hands, while flour dust drifts gold in the light behind him; before him on the ground sits an ordinary orange tabby cat — bootless yet, hatless yet — looking up at the downcast young man with bright green intelligent eyes; the mossy mill wheel turns slow water behind, hens scratch by the sacks, and the whole inheritance of the third son faces itself across two arm-lengths of packed dirt: one poor young man, one very thoughtful cat
beats.motion: the young man's shoulders sink lower over his knees while the cat's ringed tail curls and settles neatly around its forepaws, its green eyes steady on him, one ear turning as the mill wheel creaks through its slow water; flour dust drifts between them in the sun, a hen pecks past the cat without a glance, and the camera eases slowly down to the level of the two unequal heirs

beats.visual: close in the mill doorway: the orange tabby stands up on its hind legs for the first time, one forepaw laid earnestly on the seated young man's knee, whiskers forward, green eyes fixed on his face mid-speech; on the doorstep between them lie the two requested things — a pair of tall folded leather boots, small and cat-sized, and an empty canvas bag with a drawstring; the young man leans back with raised eyebrows, half doubt and half hope, flour dust haloing the door light around them, and the ordinary cat asking politely for boots is suddenly the most interesting thing the mill has ever held
beats.motion: the cat's forepaw pats the young man's knee in a slow persuading rhythm, its whiskers trembling forward with the earnest speech, tail sweeping wide behind for balance on the unaccustomed hind legs; the young man's raised eyebrows ease by degrees toward a helpless smile, his hand drifting toward the boots on the step, and the camera holds close on the negotiation at knee height

beats.visual: transformation by boots: the orange tabby stands tall in the mill yard fully equipped — tall folded leather boots on its hind legs, the wide-brimmed hat with its white plume set at an angle, the canvas bag slung across its white chest — chin high, tail curled in a proud arc, one boot set forward on the packed dirt, chin high and ready for the road; morning light gilds the plume, the young man watches open-mouthed from the crate behind, hens scatter respectfully from the small booted figure's path, and beyond the yard gate the road runs bright toward fields and the business of destiny
beats.motion: the booted cat sets off across the yard in a high-stepping strut, each tall boot planted with relish, plume nodding at every step and the slung bag swinging in time, its ringed tail carried in a proud arc behind; the hens hurry from its path in a small flustered wave, the young man's mouth opens wider behind, and the camera tracks low beside the marching boots toward the gate

beats.visual: a green warren bank at the wood's edge: the canvas bag lies open on the grass, propped with a stick, bran and fresh sow-thistle leaves scattered temptingly inside its mouth, the drawstring running back to where the booted cat lies flat behind a tussock — hat off, ears low, green eyes locked on the bag, utterly still in the way of hunting cats; at the bag's mouth a plump young rabbit sniffs the bran, one paw already on the canvas, whiskers busy; clover and morning shadows stripe the bank, and the whole scene balances on the next half-second
beats.motion: the rabbit hops its second paw into the bag mouth and leans deeper after the bran, and the instant its tail follows, the cat's paw hauls the drawstring in one long smooth pull — the canvas mouth pursing closed around a suddenly bulging, kicking bag — while the cat rises from the tussock already reaching for its hat; the stick prop tips slowly into the clover, and the camera stays low at bank level through the catch

beats.visual: the throne room in warm window light: the plump king leans forward on his great chair, crown a little askew with interest, while before him the booted cat performs a magnificent bow — plumed hat swept off and held wide, one boot pointed, the bulging canvas bag laid open at the royal footstool with the plump rabbit presented inside; courtiers' silks blur at the edges of the frame, the crimson carpet runs long between cat and throne, and the king's ringed hand is already lifting in delighted acceptance of the first gift from the Marquis of Carabas
beats.motion: the cat's bow deepens in one slow theatrical sweep, the white plume of the held-out hat brushing the carpet, tail curling with the flourish, while the king leans further forward and his ringed fingers close gently around the bag's edge to peer at the rabbit; a ripple of courtier color stirs at the frame's edges, and the camera glides down the crimson carpet toward the meeting of bow and crown

beats.visual: a tight close-up at the river boulder that leaves room for little else: the booted cat's two forepaws pressing a bundle of patched linen and grey breeches deep into the dark hollow under the stone, its plumed dark-brown hat tipped with the effort, green eyes glancing sideways up the white carriage road where a gilded coach shows small in its own dust; beyond the boulder, out on the bright water, only the young man's wet head and bare shoulders show above midstream, turned toward the bank in puzzled obedience; willow leaves frame the top of the shot, a dragonfly rests on the boulder's crown, and the hidden clothes disappear into shadow under the cat's paws
beats.motion: the cat's forepaws shove the bundled clothes deeper under the boulder in quick businesslike presses until the last pale corner sinks into shadow, then one paw rises and straightens the plumed hat by its brim in a single crisp adjust; out on the water the young man's wet head turns in a slow bewildered circle, rings widening from his shoulders, the gilded coach growing down the road, and the camera holds tight on the boulder and the vanishing evidence

beats.visual: the carriage road at the willow bend, the royal coach halted mid-journey: gilded wheels still, horses tossing, the king's crowned head leaning full out of the coach window — and in the road before it the booted cat mid-cry, up on the toes of its boots, forepaws flung wide, hat plume whipping, the picture of urgent alarm; beyond the bank the young man's head and shoulders show above the bright water, arms waving; the mown hayfields stretch gold around the halted procession, coachmen crane from their seats, and the whole summer road is stopped around one small theatrical cat
beats.motion: the cat's flung forepaws wave the coach toward the river in big urgent sweeps, boots dancing on their toes, plume whipping with each gesture, while the king's head leans further from the window and his ringed hand rises to order the halt; the horses stamp and toss against the standstill, hay dust drifting gold over the road, and the camera swings from the waving cat to the leaning crown

beats.visual: beside the royal coach in the willow shade: the young marquis — river-damp hair above the fine new coat — bowing to the plump king who beams from the coach step; within the coach window behind them a princess in rose silk leans into the light, one gloved hand at the frame, her eyes plainly and entirely on the new-made marquis; the folded pile of royal spare clothes' wrappings lies on the grass, the river glitters through the willows, and the coach door stands open in invitation
beats.motion: the young man straightens from his bow and the king's hands take his shoulders in one warm shepherding turn toward the open coach door, the princess within leaning a breath further into the window light as he approaches; the willow shade sways over coach and company, the horses settle, and the camera moves with the young man's first astonished step up toward the rose-silk glow of the doorway

beats.visual: a mown hayfield along the road ahead: the booted cat mid-dash between rows of haycocks, boots flying, plume flat with speed, bag bouncing — pausing at a knot of sun-browned mowers who lean on their scythes wide-eyed at the small booted apparition; the cat is up on a haycock before them, forepaw raised in grand instruction, hat swept back, every line of it declaiming the one required answer: these fields belong to the Marquis of Carabas; far down the road behind, the royal coach itself shows small and gilded in its own bright dust, four horses and a coachman, coming on
beats.motion: the cat springs from the road to the haycock top in one bounding scramble and wheels to face the mowers, raised forepaw sweeping the horizon of fields in a single grand instructing arc, plume shaking with emphasis; the mowers' scythes lower one by one as their heads nod, the coach dust brightens down the road, and the camera circles the small commanding figure on its golden podium

beats.visual: the rolling country seen from the coach window frame: the king's delighted profile in the foreground, crown gleaming, one ringed hand gesturing out over passing fields where mowers and reapers stand in respectful rows, hats off, scythes grounded; the fields run in great golden strips to the horizon, every one of them — as the answering mouths along the road keep saying — the land of the Marquis of Carabas; beside the king a corner of rose silk and a corner of blue court coat share the coach seat, close together, and the road runs on toward a far towered shape rising blue at the horizon's edge
beats.motion: field after field slides past the window frame in slow golden procession, each knot of mowers pulling off their hats and bowing as the coach passes, the king's gesturing hand rising higher with each answer and his beaming profile turning to the young couple beside him; the far blue towers grow at the horizon's edge, and the camera rides the window frame watching the kingdom rename itself

beats.visual: close across the corner of the great feast table: the giant of a man fills his carved chair from armrest to armrest, ruddy weathered face with its two small ivory tusks bent forward in amused interest, gold-ringed fingers the size of the candlesticks resting by a gold plate — and on the table's near corner, small as one of the goblets, stands the booted cat in its deepest courteous bow, dark-brown plumed hat swept wide, green eyes up and watchful; candle flames stand between the two faces, banners hang high in the dimness beyond, and the table's corner is the whole stage for a very small guest and a very large host
beats.motion: the cat's bow holds while its green eyes stay lifted and steady, the swept hat's plume trembling above the tablecloth, and the giant's huge ringed fingers slow their drumming to stillness as his heavy head tilts closer with amused interest, tusks catching the candlelight; the flames between them lean once with his breath, and the camera holds the corner of the table between the tiny bow and the vast leaning face

beats.visual: the great hall in uproar: a colossal lion rears alone beside the toppled carved chair, amber-eyed, mane wild, jaws wide mid-roar, one great paw sweeping gold plates from the long table — the chair's brocade cushion still spinning on the floor where its last occupant vanished into this shape — and high on a window curtain clings the booted cat, boots scrabbling, dark-brown hat crushed to its white chest, green eyes enormous, striped tail bottled huge; candle flames stream sideways with the roar, banners sway on the stone walls, and the tall leaded window rattles above the climbing speck of orange
beats.motion: the lion's roar rolls the length of the hall while its sweeping paw finishes and the scattered gold plates spin slowly to rest, the wild mane settling in waves around the huge head; up the curtain the cat's boots find one more desperate foot of height, bottled tail rigid, crushed hat pressed to its chest, and the camera trembles gently with the echo between the giant below and the clinging speck above

beats.visual: the hall gone quiet and vast: the toppled carved chair lies empty, plates scattered, and down on the stone floor in a bar of window light a small grey mouse and the booted cat face each other at a single stride's distance — the mouse up on its hind legs, whiskers twitching, proud of its clever new smallness; the cat already low in the first coil of a pounce, ears flat, green eyes lit, hind boots gathered beneath it, dark-brown hat tipped forward, front claws just spreading from the stone; the space between twitching whiskers and spreading claws is one heartbeat wide, and the candles down the long table hold perfectly still to watch
beats.motion: the cat's gathered coil releases into the leap — body unrolling low and long through the bar of window light, boots trailing, claws spreading — while the little mouse's whiskers twitch once at the shadow arriving over it; the tipped hat lifts from the cat's head and hangs in the air behind the leap, candle flames leaning with the rush, and the camera holds low and freezes on the closing heartbeat of distance

beats.visual: the castle gatehouse in golden late afternoon, banners lifting: the booted cat stands at the center of the lowered drawbridge in its finest bow yet — plumed hat swept wide, boot pointed, ringed tail in a perfect curl — welcoming the approaching royal coach up the road; behind the small majordomo the gatehouse arch opens onto a sunlit courtyard readied for a feast, and the round towers with their blue conical roofs stand tall against the warm sky; the coach comes on with its dust of gold, rose silk and blue coat visible at its window, and every stone of the castle waits under new management
beats.motion: the banners lift and roll slowly along the towers while the coach rolls up the last of the road onto the drawbridge timbers, and the cat's grand bow sweeps lower still, plume brushing the planks, tail curling tight with satisfaction; the gatehouse shadow slides over the coach as it passes within, gold dust settling behind, and the camera rises slowly up the tower face to the highest turning banner
